findings.quote: The probabilities are between $0$ and $1$, and they add up to $1$.
findings.problem: This is the lesson's only rule for a valid probability table, and it does not say whether $0$ and $1$ themselves are allowed. Read as 'strictly between', it is false at the boundary: a table may hold $P(x)=0$, and a one-value table has $P(x)=1$. A standard curriculum item asks which table is a valid probability distribution, and a student who reads 'between' as excluding the ends rejects a valid table that has a $0$ entry. The official property is $0\le P(x)\le1$.
findings.source: Checklist L27; DepEd Statistics and Probability (Grade 11) probability-distribution properties, 0 <= P(x) <= 1; reader-rules 'Added after the Sol audit' boundary test

findings.quote: Both sets above have mean $5$. Set B is more spread out.
findings.problem: The prose points to sets 'above' whose values appear only inside the invisible ILLUSTRATION comment. In the app the marker is not shown, so the student reads about Set A and Set B with no values given and cannot check either claim. The guide says the surrounding text must still teach without the image by describing the figure in words. Present since round 1 and not raised before.
